about: Every system of the mashup, one source file each. side ptr = the BepInEx plugin inside Paint the Town Red (C#); side mc = the Minecraft Fabric mod (Java, a fork of SkyCraft by chasmlol, MIT). PTR is the game on screen; Minecraft runs hidden and is the player.

columns.file: Source file, relative to the project root
columns.channels: link_channels ids it reads or writes (comma separated, '-' for none)
columns.verified: Evidence from a real run, or 'no'

rows.summary: BepInEx entry: settings, Harmony patches one class at a time, the per-frame driver
BepInEx/config/dev.ptrcraft.cfg: one entry per row of sheets/settings.json (generated)
Creates and reads/writes the shared memory (seqlocks, rings, triple buffer)

Per frame: heartbeat, level changes, take over / give back the player, input, pacing, overlay; the takeover waits until PTR's player is at rest (0.75 s, Beneath not in transition) and sends Minecraft there, again if PTR moves it before Minecraft arrives

rows.summary: PTR's colliders as Minecraft collision (exact triangles + 1/8-block voxels per 8-block region), streamed nearest the player first, built once the level has stopped changing (Beneath builds floors after loading), refreshed every 3 s; boxes and readable meshes exact, spheres and capsules tessellated; the change check ignores the player and PTR's people, and a refresh resends only regions whose content changed; regions within 160 blocks of the player, farther ones as the player gets near; the three largest colliders are logged
rows.verified: 2026-10-09: 507 regions; player walks PTR's floor and stairs

rows.summary: Colliders PTR can't hand out (272 unreadable meshes in Beneath's hub, terrain, other kinds) measured with PTR's own physics: Collider.Raycast on a 25 cm grid from six sides, surfaces merged into strips of triangles; 3 ms a frame, nearest first, kept per collider

Torches and other light-emitting Minecraft blocks as PTR lights and colliders for builds (PTR's people bump into them); with MinecraftDrawsWorld off also Minecraft's block meshes, drawn with PTR's lights
The cube where a block will go when aiming at PTR's own surfaces (Minecraft has no block there to outline); with MinecraftDrawsWorld off also the outline of Minecraft blocks
With MinecraftDrawsWorld off: arrows, tridents, dropped items and blocks, block-breaking cracks drawn in PTR
With MinecraftDrawsWorld off: Minecraft's player model (F5) and other entities and particles drawn as Unity meshes
G = PTR's use key through PTR's own interaction (buttons, Beneath items, shops)

PTR's trigger zones see the player where Minecraft is: each frame the trigger colliders its capsule overlaps get OnTriggerEnter / Stay / Exit, as do the player's own handlers; zones on PTR's people are left out (the layer matrix getter is stripped from PTR)
PTR's people as Minecraft proxies; Minecraft hits -> Enemy.Damage; PTR hits on the player -> Minecraft damage (sheets/combat_rules.json)
